flows.title: Basic Flow: Successful Account Registration
flows.terminal_outcome: A new user account is created and persisted, an authenticated session is established, and the user is redirected to the home page (/)

steps.text: The visitor opens the registration page (/register).
steps.criticality_reason: The registration page must be accessible for registration to begin.

steps.text: The frontend displays the registration form (SignUpForm).
steps.criticality_reason: The registration form must render for the user to input details.

steps.text: The visitor enters registration details: fullName, email, password, and confirmPassword.
steps.criticality_reason: Registration inputs are required to proceed with registration.

steps.text: The visitor submits the registration form.
steps.criticality_reason: Form submission triggers the registration pipeline.

steps.text: The frontend performs preliminary validation on the submitted form fields.
steps.criticality_reason: Form validation is necessary to ensure submitted data meets basic field requirements.

steps.text: The frontend sends the registration request (POST /api/auth/register) to the backend API.
steps.criticality_reason: The registration request must reach the backend API to create an account.

steps.text: The backend validates and processes the registration data according to established business rules.
steps.criticality_reason: The backend must enforce business rules to validate registration data.

steps.text: Upon successful validation, the backend persists the new user account securely and generates an authenticated session.
steps.criticality_reason: Account persistence and session generation are mandatory for successful registration.

steps.text: The backend returns a successful response containing the authentication token and created user profile data.
steps.criticality_reason: Auth token and profile data must be returned to the client.

steps.text: The frontend establishes the authenticated user session and redirects the user to the home page (/).
steps.criticality_reason: Client session establishment and redirection complete the user registration flow.

flows.title: AF-1: Client-side validation failure
flows.source_anchor: Functional Use-Case Specification / Alternative Flow / AF-1
flows.terminal_outcome: Form submission halts without calling the API, field-level error messages are displayed, and no account is created.

steps.text: The visitor enters invalid or incomplete registration details into the registration form.
steps.criticality_reason: Invalid form input is required to trigger client-side validation failure.

steps.text: The visitor submits the registration form.
If any submitted field fails preliminary validation, the frontend displays field-level error messages and halts form submission without calling the API.
steps.criticality_reason: Client must show field error messages and block the API call when validation fails.

flows.title: AF-2: Registration conflict / Duplicate account
flows.source_anchor: Functional Use-Case Specification / Alternative Flow / AF-2
flows.terminal_outcome: The backend rejects registration due to policy conflict (e.g., duplicate email), frontend displays the error message, and no duplicate account is created.

steps.text: The visitor submits registration data that conflicts with existing account policies (e.g., email already registered).
steps.criticality_reason: Conflicting registration input is required to trigger backend conflict rejection.

steps.text: The frontend sends the registration request (POST /api/auth/register) to the backend API.
steps.criticality_reason: The request must reach backend to be checked against existing accounts.

steps.text: If registration data conflicts with existing account policies, the backend rejects the request and the frontend displays the returned error message.
steps.criticality_reason: Backend conflict rejection and user notification are critical to prevent duplicate accounts.

flows.title: EF-1: Registration request failure
flows.source_anchor: Functional Use-Case Specification / Exception Flow / EF-1
flows.terminal_outcome: The frontend displays a failure notification and remains on the registration form without creating an account or establishing a session.

steps.text: The frontend sends the registration request (POST /api/auth/register) to the backend API.
steps.criticality_reason: Registration request transmission precedes network or server exception.

steps.text: If the registration request encounters an unexpected network or server error, the frontend displays a failure notification and remains on the registration form.
steps.criticality_reason: User must receive failure notification while retaining form state during unexpected errors.
